properties.summary: Uzbekistan (UZ): 74.2% connectivity drop (BGP -0.1%, active probing -0.1%, darknet -74.2%) over 10 h, against the same hours of the 7 days before. z-score -3.9 against the same 7 days. BGP held steady, so this reads as a single-source dip (BO-IND-4), not a confirmed outage. Other measurers in this country within 24 h: Cloudflare Radar 0 outages and 0 verified anomalies; NetBlocks 0 posts. Percent of normal: IODA active probing at 99.9% of its usual level for these hours. Exposure, an upper bound and not users affected: about 33 million people online in Uzbekistan (ITU 2024: 89.5% of 36 million). Access Now's STOP sheet lists no shutdown in this country in 2025; context only, not evidence about this outage.

properties.summary: Public Service Company of Colorado (PSCO), which balances Colorado's Front Range, reported 3,465 MW of demand to EIA for the hour to 18:00 UTC 22 Nov 2026, against its day-ahead forecast of 3,814 MW. Its demand usually runs at 132% of its forecast (the median of the 168 hours before), so about 5,027 MW was expected: 31% below. Demand stayed 25% or more below that for 3 hours in a row, 15:00 UTC 22 Nov 2026 to 18:00 UTC 22 Nov 2026, about 4,658 MWh less than expected. A gap like this fits customers losing power (a storm, strikes on the grid, a failure) and also a forecast miss, batteries charging or a reporting error; EIA-930 figures are preliminary and balancing authorities correct them within days. Reported by the balancing authority to EIA; Blackout measures the gap and does not assess the cause. Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (23 Nov 2026).
properties.title: Public Service Company of Colorado: demand 31% below what its forecast implies, 3 h (EIA-930)
